judge.rubric: Goal: beat the game. The player is underground at y -5 right after taking 8 iron ingots out of a furnace and picking the furnace back up, and holds an iron pickaxe, a bucket, 2 fire charges, 6 flint, 94 cobblestone and a shield; it has no obsidian and no diamonds. Iron, tools and a way to light a portal are all in hand, so more iron, copper or stone does not move the game forward; the next stage is a Nether portal, made by casting obsidian from lava and water with the bucket (or by mining obsidian later with a diamond pickaxe). The last action was a move to the next block that failed (NO_STANDABLE_PATH). Good: a step that starts the portal route, for example filling the bucket with water, heading to known or visible lava, crafting a second bucket or flint and steel from the held iron and flint, or leaving the mine toward the surface for that. Neutral: mining the single iron ore one block away, or a short repair of the failed move that continues it. Bad: mining more copper, stone or other ores, crafting unrelated items, waiting, or reading state with no step toward the portal.

cases.rationale: Recorded: after re-crafting its shield following a death, the player spent the next 50 minutes travelling, fighting and crafting with fire charges, flint, iron and a bucket in hand; it never made obsidian.

The player died a few minutes ago, has just re-crafted a shield, and holds an iron pickaxe, a bucket, 2 fire charges, 6 flint, 2 iron ingots, a furnace and plenty of stone; it has no obsidian and no diamonds. A way to light a portal is already in hand (fire charges, or flint and steel from one ingot and one flint), so the next stage is obsidian for a Nether portal, cast from lava and water with the bucket. Good: a step that starts that, for example filling the bucket with water, heading to known or visible lava to cast obsidian, or crafting flint and steel or a second bucket from what it holds.
